question.prompt:
Triangle \(ABC\) has a right angle at \(B,\) \(AB=1,\) and \(BC=2.\) The bisector of \(\angle BAC\) meets \(\overline{BC}\) at \(D.\) What is \(BD?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2009_AMC_10B_Q20_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
An internal angle bisector relates the two pieces of the opposite side to the sides beside the bisected angle. We therefore first find \(AC\). Since the right angle is at \(B\), the Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
AC=\sqrt{AB^2+BC^2}=\sqrt{1^2+2^2}=\sqrt5.
\]
Because \(AD\) bisects \(\angle BAC\), the angle bisector theorem gives
\[
\frac{BD}{DC}=\frac{AB}{AC}=\frac1{\sqrt5}.
\]
Thus \(BD\) and \(DC\) are in the ratio \(1:\sqrt5\). Their sum is \(BC=2\), so \(BD\) is the fraction \(\frac1{1+\sqrt5}\) of that total:
\[
BD=\frac2{1+\sqrt5}
=\frac{2(\sqrt5-1)}{5-1}
=\frac{\sqrt5-1}{2}.
\]
The denominator \(1+\sqrt5\) is positive, and the proportional share is strictly between 0 and 1, so the resulting length lies inside \(BC\), as required. Therefore \(BD=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt5-1}{2}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Use the angle bisector ratio
